mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of greater than 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) predicts weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND UNRATE > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a recovery in manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month + 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 70% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in nonfarm payrolls growth (PAYEMS) to below 50k new jobs per month, sustained for two months, signals labor market softening, which increases recession risk and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change < 50k for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes or not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and mortgage rates (proxied by HOUST price index) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a tightening in both monetary and credit conditions, which reduces investment and consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo MA AND HOUST > 12-mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 70% of triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A YoY increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 4% combined with a decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 5-year average signals inflationary pressure and eroded household savings, which reduces consumer purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes or not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and prompts preemptive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes or not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.
